what: Positives whose smoke has a FAILING row today, each with the measurement that put it here.
why_a_file: CI has to be green to be read, and a red build nobody can act on is a build nobody looks at. But a suite that quietly tolerates three failures is worse than one that fails: the point of naming them here is that tools/ci-smoke.mjs fails BOTH ways - if a plate not on this list starts failing, and if a plate on it starts passing. The list cannot rot in either direction.
not_an_excuse: Every entry is a real signal. None of them is a determinism question - smoke runs the CPU evaluator, and the emitter never enters it - but two are a plate that lights almost nothing at one lever setting and one is a plate that throws points off the sheet, and all three deserve the work.

buddha.rule: smoke wants kept > 5% of 20000; this is 0.5%
buddha.why: One hashed lever combination leaves almost every point declining. Predates the emitter work by at least a sweep - unchanged before and after 2026-08-23's comparison binding, which was checked rather than assumed.

qjulia.rule: smoke wants kept > 5% of 20000; this is 2.1%
qjulia.why: Same shape as buddha: a lever corner where the escape test rejects nearly everything. Also unchanged across the 2026-08-23 emitter work.

vlsi.rule: smoke wants far-out < 2% of 20000; this is 20.6%
vlsi.why: The sharpest of the three, and NOT the same class as the other two: at one lever setting the walk puts 4,127 points more than 24 units from the origin, where at defaults everything sits inside 1.30. Most likely an unguarded divide or a runaway iteration. positives/vlsi.pos.mjs has not changed since it was converted in b337609.
